question: At the beginning of a trip, the mileage odometer read \(56{,}200\) miles. The driver filled the gas tank with \(6\) gallons of gasoline. During the trip, the driver filled the tank again with \(12\) gallons of gasoline when the odometer read \(56{,}560.\) At the end of the trip, the driver filled the tank again with \(20\) gallons of gasoline; the odometer read \(57{,}060.\) To the nearest tenth, what was the car’s average miles-per-gallon for the entire trip?
solution:
The initial \(6\) gallons fill the tank before the trip begins. The tank is also full after the final refill, so the gasoline added after the initial fill replaces exactly the gasoline used during the trip. Thus the car used
\[
12+20=32\text{ gallons}.
\]
The distance traveled is the difference between the final and initial odometer readings:
\[
57{,}060-56{,}200=860\text{ miles}.
\]
Average miles per gallon means total miles divided by total gallons used, so it is
\[
\frac{860}{32}=26.875.
\]
The hundredths digit is \(7\), so rounding to the nearest tenth gives \(26.9\) miles per gallon, choice D.

nodes.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship. For example, “This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar, so there is 3/4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar.” “We paid \$75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of \$5 per hamburger."* *Expectations for unit rates in this grade are limited to non-complex fractions.
